answer: One failed audit drops an identity off the mesa. Every new attestation climbs a terrace of three checks: an automated scan, a random peer quorum, then a glacier audit that moves slowly, re-checking a random slice of old attestations each epoch. Honest agents climb once and stay: their real work passes every terrace. A farmer's 1,000 fakes must each climb all three, and the glacier eventually reaches every fake — one copied template caught in the slow sweep unravels the whole batch, forfeiting 1,000 epochs of staged work while honest cost is one climb.
